source: Ministry of Agriculture training module "ជំនិតកម្មដំណាំខ្នុរសំរាប់កសិកម្ម" (Jackfruit Cultivation Techniques for Agriculture), prepared with participation from the Santisena organization, an elderly people's association, a charitable organization, and the CRS (Catholic Relief Services) agriculture program; content compiled with reference to fruit-tree materials and Prek Leap National School of Agriculture (សាលាជាតិកសិកម្មព្រែកលៀប). Bears an AIDOC library stamp (Code/Date/Donated-by fields blank on the scanned copy).
text:
Jackfruit is a plant that most farmers like to grow because it can grow in almost any type of soil. It has many uses: the flesh and seeds of the ripe fruit are made into sweets/desserts, young (unripe) fruit is cooked as a vegetable, the trunk wood is used to make furniture and other household items, the tree serves as a windbreak and provides shade, and the leaves are used as medicine.

When choosing a jackfruit variety to plant, farmers should look for varieties that: fruit early, are resistant to disease and insect pests, produce large fruit, have thick husks with abundant flesh, taste sweet, are fragrant, have well-formed fruit shape, come from a clear/known source (reliable parent stock), and are suited for sale in higher-value markets. Note: one phrase describing the desired flesh texture was only partly legible in the source and has been omitted rather than guessed at.
